reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational concept of behavior as a molar phenomenon unifies action and intentionality into a structured morphism. The behavioral pattern morphism (BPM) formalizes how behavior is not just a simple act but a structured sequence linking a goal (G) to a means (M), expressed as a pattern. This is mathematically modeled as a conditional probability P(G|B,M) where B represents the behavioral event. The molar structure (MS) extends this by embedding the behavioral trajectory (e.g., rat running) into a space of possible paths (A), allowing for probabilistic path selection. The communion (CM) primitive introduces the relational aspect, where behavior is not isolated but embedded in a network of interactions with means objects. These three primitives form a triadic kernel: BPM → MS → CM. Failure modes occur when any component lacks structure: absence of pattern (BPM), lack of trajectory (MS), or disconnection from means (CM). Dualities emerge in the symmetry between goal-seeking and means-usage, while the failure modes reveal the fragility of the system under structural collapse.
